info.title: The Data-Bridge (TDB)
info.description: A secure, auditable API layer over your existing data sources. Register a data source once, query it anywhere.

post.description: Authenticate with username and password. Returns a Bearer JWT for use on all protected endpoints.
Creates a new DB-managed API key. The raw key is returned once and cannot be retrieved again.
Revokes the current key and issues a replacement with the same name. The new raw key is returned once.

put.description: Override the rate limit for a specific key. Pass null for requests_per_minute to reset to the server default.
Update the RBAC role assigned to a DB-managed API key.

Restrict which MCP tools a key may call and is listed. Pass null for tools to allow all tools (default). An unknown tool name is rejected with 400. Calls to disallowed tools return a JSON-RPC tool-error response.

put.summary: Set a key's Lean Mode default
put.description: Default Lean Mode for MCP calls made with this key. A tool call's own arguments still win, and the key's setting wins over TDB_LEAN_MODE. Send {} to clear it. An invalid value is rejected with 400.

schema.title: Response List Sources V1 Sources Get

post.description:
Register a data source so it can be queried through TDB.

**source_type** values are validated against the internal connector
registry (ADR-001 step 2). New types can be added by an overlay
package calling `tdb.connectors.registry.register()` at startup.

get.summary: Get details of a specific source (UUID or name)

delete.summary: Remove a registered source (UUID or name)

get.summary: Inspect column names and types for a registered source (UUID or name)
get.description:
Returns the column names and inferred types for the registered source.
No rows are returned — schema introspection only.

Every annotation stored for the source.

Targets are checked when they are written, but a schema moves underneath
them: a column that is renamed or dropped leaves an annotation that matches
nothing and says nothing, surfacing only as a description that quietly stops
appearing in `schema_source`. `?validate=true` re-runs the write-time check
against the live schema and marks each annotation `stale` with the reason.

As on the write path, `validated: false` means the source could not be read
— never that nothing matched. An unreachable database is not evidence that
an annotation is wrong, so nothing is flagged stale on that path.

parameters.name: validate

schema.description: Re-check each stored annotation against the source's live schema and flag the ones that no longer match. Off by default: it turns a registry read into a round-trip to the source.
schema.title: Validate

parameters.description: Re-check each stored annotation against the source's live schema and flag the ones that no longer match. Off by default: it turns a registry read into a round-trip to the source.

schema.title: Response List Annotations V1 Sources  Ref  Annotations Get

put.description:
Upserts each annotation. Existing entries for the same table/column are
replaced; annotations not mentioned are left alone. Use DELETE to remove one.

Targets are validated against the live schema by default: an annotation on a
misspelled column never matches anything and would otherwise fail silently,
surfacing as "the description I wrote isn't showing up" long after the typo.
If the source cannot be reached the write still succeeds and the response
reports `validated: false` — an unreachable database is not evidence that an
annotation is wrong.

parameters.name: validate

schema.description: Check each table/column against the source's live schema and reject the request if one does not exist. Set false to annotate a column that has not shipped yet.
schema.title: Validate

parameters.description: Check each table/column against the source's live schema and reject the request if one does not exist. Set false to annotate a column that has not shipped yet.

post.summary: Run a SQL query against a registered data source
post.description:
Execute a **read-only** SQL SELECT against a registered source.

### Example
```json
{
  "source_id": "abc-123",
  "sql": "SELECT * FROM orders LIMIT 50",
  "limit": 50
}
```

Use the table name that matches the connector: CSV sources are exposed as
`data`, while database connectors (Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake)
take the **actual table name** from the source's `connection.table` — the
SQL is passed through to the database unchanged apart from an appended
`LIMIT`, so there is no `data` alias for database sources.

Model Context Protocol endpoint (JSON-RPC 2.0).

Connects Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP clients directly to
the registered data source without extra configuration.

Supported methods: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, and
from 2026-07-28 `server/discover`

get.description: Return all view definitions loaded from TDB_VIEWS_DIR.

schema.title: Response List Views V1 Views Get

post.description:
Run a named view, supplying values for any declared parameters.

### Example
```json
{"parameters": {"status": "pending"}, "limit": 100}
```

get.summary: Verify audit log hash chain integrity
get.description:
Reads the audit log and verifies every signed entry's hash and chain link.

Returns ``{"valid": true, "entries": N}`` when the chain is intact,
or ``{"valid": false, "error": "...", "at_seq": N}`` if tampering is detected.

Legacy entries written before hash-chaining was enabled are skipped.

schema.title: Response Audit Verify V1 Audit Verify Get

get.summary: Verify the live log and every sealed segment
get.description:
Verifies each sealed segment, the live log, and the anchors linking them.

``/verify`` proves the *live* log has not been altered, but each segment
restarts its chain from genesis, so it cannot prove a whole segment was not
removed. This walks the ``chain_anchor`` entries to check the sequence is
complete.

Pruning the oldest segments is a supported retention action and stays valid;
a gap in the middle does not.

schema.title: Response Audit History V1 Audit History Get

post.summary: Seal the audit log into a segment now
post.description:
Seals the live audit log into a timestamped segment and starts a fresh chain.

The segment keeps its chain intact and stays independently verifiable. TDB
never deletes a segment — removing old ones is the operator's decision.

Returns ``{"rotated": true, "segment": "...", "entries_sealed": N}``, or
``{"rotated": false, "reason": "log is empty"}`` when there is nothing to seal.

schema.title: Response Audit Rotate V1 Audit Rotate Post

post.summary: Export audit log to a SIEM destination
post.description:
Ships audit entries the destination has not yet received, to Splunk HEC or S3. Each destination keeps its own cursor, so a scheduled export is incremental rather than re-sending the whole log every run. Configure Splunk via TDB_SPLUNK_HEC_URL / TDB_SPLUNK_HEC_TOKEN, or S3 via TDB_S3_BUCKET. An unconfigured destination is a no-op and reports `disabled`. Pass `since_seq=0` to re-send history.

Runs synchronously by default and returns what it shipped. Pass `wait=false` to get 202 immediately and let it run in the background — read the outcome afterwards from GET /v1/audit/export/status, which reports `last_run` per destination. Either way a destination exports one run at a time: an overlapping call gets 409, because two runs share a cursor and would ship the same entries twice.

parameters.name: since_seq

schema.description: Ignore the stored cursor and export everything after this seq. Use 0 to re-send the entire log.
schema.title: Since Seq

parameters.description: Ignore the stored cursor and export everything after this seq. Use 0 to re-send the entire log.

parameters.name: wait

schema.description: Wait for the export to finish and return its result. Pass false to return 202 immediately and run it in the background.
schema.title: Wait

parameters.description: Wait for the export to finish and return its result. Pass false to return 202 immediately and run it in the background.

409.description: An export to this destination is already running.

get.description: Liveness probe — used by Docker / k8s health checks.

Report the running version and build SHA (authenticated).

Used to confirm a deployment's exact patch level after a security update —
e.g. an operator comparing against the latest released image, with no
phone-home. The unauthenticated `/` banner also carries `version`.

table.title: Table
table.description: Table this applies to. Omit for a single-table source.

column.title: Column
column.description: Column this applies to. Omit to describe the table itself.

rate_limit.title: Rate Limit
rate_limit.description: Requests per minute. Omit to use server default (TDB_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT).

role.title: Role
role.description: RBAC role for this key: 'read', 'readwrite', or 'admin'. Defaults to 'read' — a key handed to an AI agent should not be able to manage keys or sources unless that is asked for.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Max rows to return (default 100). The ceiling is the deployment's TDB_MAX_ROWS setting (default 1,000); a larger value is rejected with 400 rather than silently clamped.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Max rows (default 1,000, or TDB_MAX_ROWS if lower). Above the deployment's TDB_MAX_ROWS is refused with 400.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: List of allowed MCP tool names for this key. Pass null to allow all tools (default). Example: ['query_source', 'schema_source']

lean.title: Lean
lean.description: true = table rows and {column: type} schemas.

max_cell_chars.title: Max Cell Chars
max_cell_chars.description: Cut longer text cells (min 50; 0 = off). Lossy.

requests_per_minute.title: Requests Per Minute
requests_per_minute.description: Set to null to fall back to the server default.
